lines.text: Here's how to build a Claude skill, in sixty seconds.
A skill is a set of instructions Claude picks up on its own, when your request needs it.
Let's build one, step by step.
Say you want Claude to write your pull request descriptions, the same way every time.
Step one: in dot claude slash skills, make a folder named after the skill. P R description.
Step two: inside it, add one file: skill dot M D.
At the top, a name, and a description of when to use it.
Below that, the instructions, in plain English: run git diff, then write three sections. What, why, and changes.
Claude reads only each skill's name and description up front. When your request matches, it loads the full file and follows it.
Same format, every time. Just keep the description specific, or Claude won't know when to use it.
